**Finding submitted — WARRANTY: deviation (fallback cure).**

- **What I inspected:** Article XIII in full (13.1 mutual reps, 13.2 RevMed IP/title reps, 13.3 RevMed covenants, 13.4 mutual covenants, 13.5 disclaimer, 13.6 closing conditions), plus document-wide searches for "software", "Deliverable", "services", "professional and workmanlike", and the Research/Development Plan machinery.
- **Gap:** RevMed's reps are title/IP assurances given only as of the Execution Date. There is no conformance warranty for anything RevMed delivers, no warranted period for its performance, and no repair/replace or refund remedy — and Section 13.5 affirmatively excludes anything not expressly stated in Article XIII, so all four fallback elements fail.
- **Cure:** One insert as new Section 13.3(e) (inside Article XIII, so the 13.5 carve-out preserves it): 90-day software-to-documentation conformance, 30-day conformance of RevMed's services to the applicable Research Plan or Development Plan, with repair/replacement, re-performance or refund.
- **Deliberately not added:** the preferred 12-month period, workmanlike standard, and no-malicious-code terms (other-level extras), and compliance with Applicable Law, which is already covered by the mutual covenant in Section 13.4(b) — noted in the rationale rather than duplicated.
